engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
title: Streaming load pattern: availableNow with a checkpoint into Bronze
objective_text: Fix a Structured Streaming load into Bronze so that its checkpoint and trigger(availableNow=True) make each run take only new files, with the right column types.
scenario: Order files land in Files/landing/orders once a day, and a stream loads them into bronze.orders. Someone named the checkpoint folder after the time the load starts, so every run, including a rerun after a failure, loads every old file again. Finance also noticed amount arrives as text.
starting_environment: Two JSON Lines files in Files/landing/orders and the duplicating stream as answer.py.
required: bronze.orders holds each order from the landing files once, however many times the load runs.
order_id is an integer, customer is text and amount is a double.

expected.description: bronze.orders has orders 1 to 5, once each.

verifies: After your load runs, and again after it runs a second time, bronze.orders holds each landed order once, with the right types, on this PC.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in Fabric: every stream here runs as availableNow, taking what has arrived and stopping. A stream left running with a processingTime trigger isn't shown.
New files arriving between runs: the files are fixed, so the second run finds nothing new.
Running the stream in production, which Fabric's guidance puts in a Spark job definition with a retry policy.

validation.fail: bronze.orders doesn't hold the landed orders: read the whole folder.

validation.pass: The columns and types are right.
validation.fail: A column or type is off: set it in the schema.

validation.pass: A second run added nothing: the checkpoint remembered the files.
validation.fail: A second run changed bronze.orders: a rerun must skip files it already loaded.

hints: Run it twice and compare the row counts. What does the stream use to remember the files it took?
The checkpointLocation is where the stream remembers which files it has taken. It must be the same folder on every run.
A file stream's columns and types come from the schema you give it.
.trigger(availableNow=True) takes everything that has arrived, writes it and stops.
explanation: A file stream with a checkpoint remembers which files it has processed, so a rerun or the next day's run takes only new files. trigger(availableNow=True) processes what's available and then stops, which suits a scheduled Bronze load. The checkpoint folder has to stay the same between runs: a new one each run forgets everything and reloads every file. File streams need an explicit schema, which also fixes the column types.
troubleshooting: A second run doubles the rows: the checkpointLocation changes on each run, so the stream forgets what it loaded.
amount is text: set DoubleType for it in the schema.
reset: Reset removes bronze.orders and the checkpoint, and puts the starter back.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-06 (lakehouse-streaming-data): format("delta")-style sinks with option("checkpointLocation", "Files/checkpoint") and toTable; production streams in Spark job definitions with a retry policy. trigger(availableNow=True) is from Apache Spark's guide; Fabric's page doesn't mention it.
No hidden data: the files are the same on every run, so the checks are practice data, types and rerun safety.
The PySpark lab reads files only as streams (spark.read reads Delta tables), so the starter is a stream with the two faults rather than a batch load.
